I'm just venting a moment, and I couldn't find a better place to do it. I was tasked with submitting the electronic 1094/1095-C forms where I work. We found ourselves in the position we are in because the company that handles our payroll was unwilling to allow us to submit our 1095C with the Offer of Coverage code that applied to our situation. We have too many employees to submit them by paper, so we have to follow the IRS guidelines to submit electronically.

Now, normally this wouldn't be a problem: Take a CSV spreadsheet of information, convert it into an XML, send it on its way. Unfortunately, since the CSV was not accurate (thanks to the payroll company) I had to export all the information to PDFs for HR to review and make corrections. Then, I couldn't use Acrobat to bring the data back to a CSV (or other type) file. So, I had to manually click through and export the form data for 867 1095C forms into XML so that I could extract the data and get into a single XML file.

Once I got the file ready to test, I found that the XML elements have to be in a particular order. So, I had to adjust the code to handle that. Once that was finished, I found that there were more regulatory hurdles to overcome.

Even though I didn't develop software (I used PowerShell scripts and JAVAScript) I had to get a software ID. I didn't find that out until two weeks before the deadline. The software developer requirements are irritating because I have to pass 4 tests to submit, AND I have to submit my code to the IRS!

Again, I'm just ranting, but this whole ordeal has been very trying.
